limits: Chapter gives no experiments of its own; ADAS numbers are quoted from the original paper.
The 'under a second' latency claim is from unnamed tutorials.
A2A is described as early-stage with open security questions; may have dated.
Supply-chain tools are stubs returning fixed strings, so the multiagent gain is asserted, not measured.
Single-agent example uses model gpt-5 while the multiagent one uses gpt-4o.
practices: Begin with a single agent and add agents only as needed for performance (How Many Agents Do I Need?).
Prefer a single agent when latency is critical, since multiagent adds exchanges between agents.
Before going multiagent, group tools hierarchically or use semantic tool selection with a vector database (cites Chapter 5).
If those fall short, decompose tools into specialist agents with narrower prompts and toolsets.
Apply principles: task decomposition, specialization, parsimony, coordination, robustness, efficiency (Principles for Adding Agents).
Use manager coordination for structured settings; democratic for fairness and robustness; hierarchical for large systems.
Use actor-critic when evaluation is easier than generation and the extra compute is acceptable.
Use Redis Stream for prototypes, Kafka for durable replayable logs, NATS for low-latency edge use.
Use an actor framework (Ray, Orleans, Akka) when agents exceed about 10-20 or workloads vary.
Use Temporal for durable long-running agent workflows; Airflow only for batch or time-triggered work.

terms.definition: encourages adding only the minimal number of agents necessary to achieve the desired functionality and performance
each agent within the system is given equal decision-making power, with the goal of reaching consensus
one or more agents are designated as managers that are responsible for overseeing and directing the actions of subordinate agents
a multitiered approach combining centralized and decentralized control through a structured hierarchy
a lightweight form of evaluation-driven iteration: the actor generates candidates, the critic accepts or rejects against a rubric
large numbers of simple agents operate with minimal individual intelligence but collectively give rise to emergent behavior through local interactions
a machine-readable JSON descriptor that each agent publishes to advertise its identity, capabilities, endpoints, and supported authentication methods
Automated Design of Agentic Systems; Meta Agent Search has a meta-agent write, test and archive agent code
